brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut: they keep 5.9% profit vs peers' 3.8%, and their cash is stuck 25 days longer — offer 15-day faster payment in exchange.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price reduction across rigid plastic packaging.
priceAsk.target: Target a saving of roughly ₹55–80 lakh per year on our ₹5.49 Cr spend.
priceAsk.basis: They keep 5.9% profit vs 3.8% for similar firms — there's room in their price. Market asking prices for a 28 mm PP cap run ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95), with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume — so a double-digit cut is fair.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (move from 30 days to 15 days after receipt) in return for the price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days earlier costs us ₹22.57 L in cash tied up, but their borrowing rate is 12.19% — so saving us 10–15% on price is worth far more to us than the interest cost to them.

brief.financialLeverage: They're healthy — rated CRISIL A+ / Stable, making ₹937.60 Cr revenue and keeping 5.9% profit (well above the 3.8% peer median). But their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d for similar firms, so cash is tighter than it looks. We're 0.59% of their revenue — small but not tiny. They borrow money at about 12.19%, so faster payment is valuable to them. Their Altman Z-score is 2.17 (grey zone) — not distressed, but not bulletproof either — so push firmly on price, but don't squeeze so hard we destabilise a decent supplier.

evidence.point: They keep more profit than peers
Their cash is stuck longer than similar firms
We are a small but visible customer
They borrow at a high rate
Market asking price for 28 mm PP cap shows room
evidence.figure: ₹0.55–1.20/pc typical ₹0.85–0.95; headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms — a very strong second source.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed leader in rigid plastic (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) — pails, containers, pharma packaging — robust alternate for bottles and closures.

risks: Altman Z-score 2.17 puts them in the grey zone — healthy today, but not a huge margin for error. Don't push so hard the relationship or their stability breaks.
Our spend is only 0.59% of their revenue — we're not a make-or-break customer, so they may walk if the ask is too aggressive.
They already pay their own suppliers slower than peers (49d vs 37d) — asking for longer payment terms for us won't fly; the trade has to be faster payment for a price cut.

Market asking prices show 'MARKET-FAIR' with only modest headroom at higher volume — a 10–15% cut is ambitious but justifiable given their profit margin; going beyond that may need a volume commitment or spec change.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to talk about bringing our price down by 10–15% — you're keeping 5.9% profit vs the industry's 3.8%, and we're ready to pay you 15 days faster to help your cash flow in return.
